og.title: Trim video online — in your browser, nothing uploaded
og.description: Pick the start and end on a preview, keep the quality, download an MP4. Free, no watermark, no upload.
hero.title: Trim a video online
hero.lead: Cut the dead air off the start, stop before the awkward ending, or pull one moment out of a long recording. Set the start and end on a preview of your video and download the result as a standard MP4 — at the original quality, or squeezed under a file size at the same time. Everything runs on your own device, so a two-gigabyte file doesn't need a two-gigabyte upload before you can even begin.
how.s1: Drop your video onto the tool above, or browse for it. It opens instantly, however large it is, because it stays on your device.
how.s2: Move the Start and End sliders. The preview jumps to each point as you drag, and the line underneath tells you exactly how much you're keeping.
how.s3: Choose Quality to keep the picture as it is, or Target size to trim and fit under a limit in one go. Press Trim video and download the MP4.
prose.p1: Many quick trimmers cut only at the nearest keyframe — the points a video file is allowed to start playing from, often a second or more apart — so your cut lands somewhere near where you asked. This tool re-encodes the kept range instead, which means the cut is exactly where the slider was, to a tenth of a second, and the output is a clean MP4 that plays everywhere. On modern browsers the encoding uses your device's own video hardware and typically finishes faster than the clip would take to play.
prose.p2: Because the trimmer shares its engine with the compressor, you can do both at once: pick a range, switch to Target size, and the tool works out how much detail fits your seconds into 10, 25 or 50 MB — handy for a Discord clip or an email attachment. Nothing about your file is sent anywhere. There is no server that could receive it; you can watch the browser's network tab stay silent while it works.
faq.a1: In Quality mode the kept range is re-encoded at a high setting — for most phone and screen recordings you won't tell the difference. Re-encoding is what makes the cut land exactly where you asked instead of snapping to the nearest keyframe. If you need a smaller file too, Target size mode trims and compresses together.
faq.q2: Is there a maximum file size or length?
faq.a2: Nothing is uploaded, so there's no upload limit. Files of several gigabytes work in Chrome and Edge, which process the video with your device's hardware. Formats that need the compatibility engine — AVI, WMV and other older containers — are limited to 1.5 GB and can't be previewed for trimming; convert those to MP4 first.
faq.q3: Can I cut the middle out of a video, or join clips?
faq.a3: Not yet — this tool keeps one continuous range and everything outside it is dropped. To remove a section from the middle, trim the two halves separately for now. Joining clips is planned.
faq.q4: Is my video uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: No. The whole process — reading the file, previewing it, cutting and encoding — happens in your browser on your own device. There is no server involved, no account, and the result carries no watermark.
